summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: This bill amends the Family Law Amendment (Information Sharing) Bill 2023 to strengthen protections and oversight in the enhanced information sharing framework under the Family Law Act 1975.

The amendments lower the threshold for court orders to require only a suspicion of abuse, neglect, or family violence, make it mandatory for information sharing agencies to advise the court on disclosure risks, and expand notification requirements when disclosing a notifier's identity.
The bill also adds a second statutory review of the amendments, to be conducted as soon as practicable after 3 years from commencement, in addition to the existing review after 12 months.
changes: Amends paragraphs 67ZBD(2)(a) and 67ZBE(2)(a) to require only a suspicion of abuse, neglect, or family violence for court orders.
Changes 'may' to 'must' in subsection 67ZBG(2) to make it mandatory for information sharing agencies to provide advice to the court.
Expands subsection 67ZBH(4) to require the court to notify and consider advice from information sharing agencies when disclosing a notifier's identity who is also a party.
Adds a requirement for a review of the amendments to be conducted as soon as practicable after 3 years following commencement.
summary.affected: The amendments affect the family courts, information sharing agencies, and parties to family law proceedings, including notifiers of suspected child abuse or family violence.

divisions.question: The majority voted in favour of a [motion](https://www.openaustralia.org.au/senate/?id=2023-10-19.61.1) to pass the bills. In parliamentary jargon, they voted to read them for a third time. This means that the bill will now return to the House of Representatives, where our MPs will decide on whether they agree with the [Senate amendments](https://parlinfo.aph.gov.au/parlInfo/search/display/display.w3p;query=Id:legislation/billhome/display.w3p;query=Id%3A%22legislation%2Fsched%2Fr7011_sched_20d5e2f4-d8ff-4ed8-a047-5285cbbe7b1d%22;rec=0) and so allow the bills to become law. ### What does the bill do? speeches.speaker: Tony Burke
speeches.brief: The Northern Australia Infrastructure Facility Amendment (Miscellaneous Measures) Bill 2023, the Infrastructure Australia Amendment (Independent Review) Bill 2023, the Family Law Amendment Bill 2023, the Family Law Amendment (Information Sharing) Bill 2023, and the Crimes and Other Legislation Amendment (Omnibus) Bill 2023 were referred to the Federation Chamber for further consideration at the adjournment of the debate on the second reading of each bill.
